title: Installing a Landmine Agent on macOS

blocks.text: This article provides instructions for installing a Landmine Agent on the macOS platform using the CLI.
Beginning with version 4.32, the following changes apply:

blocks.item: You can install Landmine Agents using the .pkg file even if the endpoints have existing Landmine Agents. The new version of Landmine Agent overwrites the previous installation and moves it to the /opt/ directory regardless of the previous location. The service name is retained from the previous installation regardless of the current configuration.

The uninstall.sh script is no longer part of the Landmine Agent installation packages. The existing uninstall.sh script file is removed when the Landmine Agent is updated. Uninstallation of Landmine Agents via the Deception Admin Portal and manual removal using the command (sudo <PATH_TO_updater> landmine remove) continue to be supported.

blocks.text: Before installing a Landmine Agent, ensure that you have:

blocks.item: A Mac computer with macOS Ventura (version 13) or later.

Network connectivity from the system where the agent is installed to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal instance on port 443. This connection is proxy-aware, and you can optionally define a list of proxies for the agent to connect through.
(Optional) Enabled Full Disk Access for the agent. This is required to use the Defense Evasion, file decoy events, brute force login detections, and process tree functionality in other features.
Steps to grant Full Disk Access for manual installs.
In the macOS endpoint, go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access.
Enable the toggle for XPCServerApp.app.
Reboot the machine.
Snippet to grant Full Disk Access that can be added to the MDM profile.
A profile with a Full Disk Access grant must be deployed before installing Landmine Agents. After installing the Landmine Agent, the machine must be rebooted.

<key>SystemPolicyAllFiles</key> <array> <dict> <key>Allowed</key> <true/> <key>CodeRequirement</key> <string>identifier "com.zscaler.deception.XPCServerApp" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7</string> <key>Identifier</key> <string>com.zscaler.deception.XPCServerApp</string> <key>IdentifierType</key> <string>bundleID</string> <key>StaticCode</key> <false/> </dict> </array>

blocks.text: To install a Landmine Agent on macOS:

blocks.item: Download the macOS installer (Intel or Apple Silicon) file from the Deception Admin Portal.
Run the following command in a terminal to create /tmp/landmine.txt with required permissions:
sudo /bin/sh -c 'set -e; rm -f /tmp/landmine.txt; umask 077; /bin/cat > /tmp/landmine.txt'
Copy the values (Deception Admin Portal's instance name and the agent registration token) from the Download Landmine Agent window and paste them into the text file (one value per line):
<deception-admin-portal-instance-name> <agent-registration-token>
(Optional) If a proxy is required, add a third line containing a comma-separated list of proxy URLs:
<deception-admin-portal-instance-name> <agent-registration-token> <proxy-URL-1>,<proxy-URL-2>
Press Ctrl+D when finished.
The /tmp/landmine.txt file is created as a root-owned file with mode 600, preventing non-root users from reading or modifying the file.
Run the following command in a terminal from the path where the .pkg file is downloaded:
For Intel-based macOS endpoints:
sudo installer -pkg Landmine_Intel.pkg -target /
For Apple Silicon-based macOS endpoints:
sudo installer -pkg Landmine_AppleSilicon.pkg -target /

blocks.text: To configure proxies for macOS, add the proxy definition to the text file (/tmp/landmine.txt). To configure multiple proxies, add a list of proxies separated by commas.

When the Landmine Agent starts, it attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal using the list of proxies in a sequence from left to right. Finally, the agent tries to connect directly without a proxy.
After you run the command, the Landmine Agent connects to the portal using one of the following methods:

blocks.item: Connects via http://user:password@proxy-server:8888/proxy.
Connects via http://proxy-server:3128/proxy.

blocks.text: If all of the above methods fail, the agent attempts to connect to the portal using a direct no-proxy connection.
You can configure proxies using the following URL format:
If the username and password have special characters (e.g., Username = user#2211 and password = pass@123), you must URL-encode them. For example:

blocks.item: http://192.0.2.2:3128/: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.2 and port number = 3128.
http://proxy-server:8888/: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server and port number = 8888.
http://proxyuser:proxypassword@192.0.2.18:3128/: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.18, port number = 3128, username = proxyuser, and password = proxypassword.
http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888/: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server, port number = 8888, username= user#2211, and password = pass@123.
